newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX shrugs of French woes, hits records.
newsitem.headline: German DAX shrugs of French woes, hits records.

text.p: German shares shrugged off early nerves following the unexpected left-wing victory in the French parliamentary elections to surge to fresh record highs in bourse trade, albeit on thin volumes.
The blue chip DAX index surged past old records to end the bourse session up 55.67 points, or 1.55 percent, at 3,657.86 points. Earlier the DAX set a new intraday high of 3,661.01.
"The mood really changed once floor trading began," said one dealer, referring to the weak start to pre-bourse trade amid disquiet after the French election outcome.
"But this was no real euphoria," he cautioned.
"With volumes as low as this, anything can happen," said another dealer, noting that business was markedly limited because U.S. and British markets are closed.
"People always want to be in on the rallies," he said.

The chemical sector was to the fore after Swiss pharmaceuticals giant Roche Holding Ltd said it planned to buy the privately owned German firm Boehringer Mannheim, adding to interest in a sector already in vogue for technical reasons.
The DAX 100 chemical sector index advanced 2.2 percent.
Bayer AG was up 2.52 marks at 68.37 marks while Hoechst AG rose 2.55 marks to 69.15 marks.

At the same time, dealers said there was still widespread talk of the need for a correction from the share market's current lofty heights, but noted that this was only likely to happen if other markets, chiefly Wall Street, led the way.
"As long as Wall Street's closed, we're not really going anywhere," a dealer said.
